issues.legal_issue: A dispute over a Collector’s failure to award statutory interest in compensation redetermination proceedings is not referable to a civil court under the land-acquisition reference procedure and may be challenged by a constitutional writ.
material_facts: Land was acquired for a public purpose, and a court later enhanced compensation for another landowner whose land had been acquired under the same notification.
The landowners applied to the Collector for redetermination of their compensation on the basis of that court award.
The Collector redetermined their compensation but did not award interest under Sections 28 or 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and rejected their request for interest.
The landowners challenged the refusal to award interest by filing writ petitions.
The government argued that the landowners had to seek a reference to the civil court under Sections 28A(3) and 18 instead of filing writ petitions.
issues.conclusion: Non-award of interest under Sections 28 or 34 is not a matter referable to the civil court under Section 18 or Section 28A(3); an aggrieved person may challenge that omission by a writ petition under Article 226. The High Court was right to entertain the writ petitions, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 28A(3) permit a civil-court reference only for the specified disputes concerning measurement, compensation, the person to whom compensation is payable, and apportionment; non-award of interest is not among them. Interest under Sections 28 and 34 is statutory and mandatory when their conditions are met, and its non-award is therefore not made referable merely because awarded interest may form part of an award. The Court relied on Shree Vijay Cotton & Oil Mills Ltd. v. State of Gujarat, (1991) 1 SCC 262, which explains the statutory character of interest and that procedural requirements should not obstruct substantive rights, and Delhi Development Authority v. Mahender Singh, (2009) 5 SCC 339, concerning interest in proceedings under Article 226.

rule.if: land_acquisition_redetermination_proceeding and collector_redetermined_compensation and collector_omitted_interest and claimant_challenged_interest_omission and reference_process_limited_to_enumerated_disputes

predicates.land_acquisition_redetermination_proceed: The proceeding concerns redetermination of compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.collector_redetermined_compensation: The Collector determined compensation for the claimant in the redetermination proceeding.
predicates.collector_omitted_interest: The Collector did not award interest sought by the claimant on the compensation.
predicates.claimant_challenged_interest_omission: The claimant challenged the Collector’s failure to award interest.
predicates.reference_process_limited_to_enumerated_: The available reference process is confined to disputes about land measurement, the compensation amount, the person entitled to compensation, or apportionment.

issues.definition: When a compensation redetermination proceeding involves a Collector’s omission of interest and the claimant challenges that omission, the claimant may bring the challenge by constitutional writ if the reference process is confined to the enumerated compensation disputes.
